title: Source-translation and exhaustion-shape stress of the weighted fractional shell
question: Does the local Kubo--Mori weighted theta=1/2 shell remain controlled when the measured source site and the selected bond are translated across edge and square shapes?
method: Use actual-Q3 V=2 edge cutoffs 3,4,5,6 with both sites and V=4 square cutoff 2 with all four sites and all four bond terms.
For every selected bond construct the doubled-bond Gibbs probabilities and the Kubo--Mori logarithmic-mean weights at beta 1/2 and 1.
Retain every prefix position in both split orders, time signs and history adjoints and evaluate the theta=1/2 weighted phase bound.
Rebuild the complete table in a non-importing independent lane, compare global, regime and per-bond maxima, and compile Lean R369.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 8601/8601 assertions over 2816 contexts; integrated passes 104/104 and Lean R369 passes. The maximum weighted fractional norm is 1.208758407679001 with bound 0.4029194692263337 and change-to-bound ratio 0.3868613066541026. Edge per-cutoff maxima are 0.0896064105, 0.2005166806, 0.3423910272 and 1.2087584077 for d=3..6; square bond maxima range from 3.1737537048e-08 to 3.5303692708e-08. The largest primary-independent difference is 4.219e-15.
decision_reason: The weighted finite shell is stable across all translated square bonds and source sites, so the R-368 suppression is not tied to one selected bond. However, the edge cutoff sequence grows substantially from d=3 to d=6. This keeps the regulator-uniform theorem open and identifies the need for an analytic cutoff-independent Dirichlet collar.

adversarial_review.check: All four square bond terms and the edge bond are selected explicitly; no last-bond-only convention is hidden.
Every site in the edge and square fixtures is measured, while unlisted shapes remain out of scope.
Every position in both forward and reverse split orders is included.
The d=3..6 edge maxima grow markedly and are not promoted to divergence or uniformity.
The Kubo--Mori probabilities come from the finite doubled local bond, not the full interacting KMS state.
The independent lane rebuilds model, weights, witnesses, spectra and prefixes without importing primary R-369.
Common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Derive an analytic local Kubo--Mori/Dirichlet collar with cutoff-independent weights and then test source-complete exhaustion shapes; register any rigorous lower-growth obstruction separately.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite translation/shape stress only. The local doubled-bond Gibbs proxy is not a global KMS state and the cutoff, volume, source and shape uniform gates remain open, as do common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A.
no_overclaim: R-369 records finite position stability together with finite cutoff growth; it neither proves a uniform theorem nor supplies a QFT closure.
